title: Bill Medicare only if s 19AA allows it (doctors first registered after a set date)
what: Medicare benefits are not payable for services by medical practitioners who first became registered after a set date unless an exception in s 19AA applies, such as recognised specialist or general practice qualifications.

sources.title: Health Insurance Act 1973
sources.quote: 19AA Medicare benefits not payable in respect of services rendered by certain medical practitioners (1) A medicare benefit is not payable in respect of a professional service, rendered after the commencement of this section, if the person who rendered the service: (a) first became a registered medical practitioner on or after 1 November 1996;

reach.condition: if its doctors render services that would attract Medicare benefits

assessment.summary: Medicare benefits are not payable for services by medical practitioners who first became registered after a set date unless an exception in s 19AA applies, such as recognised specialist or general practice qualifications.

marks.reason: Doctors registered after the set date cannot bill Medicare until they meet s 19AA, which shapes where and how new practitioners can start.
Restricts where newer doctors can practise with Medicare billing.
